why: The criterion holds for the whole verifier brief. I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1–5 require exact stdout followed by one newline, which matches "prints exactly … followed by a newline", and check 1 also requires exit 0. Check 5 reads `\t` as the two-character JSON escape, which is what the literal text `[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]` says. Check 6 requires that npm test exits 0 and that some test runs the CLI with --tsv on tab-containing input and asserts on the output. That matches "npm test exits 0" and "runs … with --tsv … and checks its output". Check 7 requires only that README.md mentions --tsv and shows an example command line using it. The stricter parts sit under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)": the proofs' test:cli script, the README's exact form and wording, and the probes for argument position, \r\n endings and non-goals.
